hints.title: Subarray Enumeration Obstacle
hints.text: Generating all O(N^2) subarrays and finding each minimum takes quadratic or cubic time. How can you invert the problem by determining how many subarrays have a given element as their minimum?

hints.title: Contribution Window Invariant
hints.text: Element arr[i] is the minimum of a subarray [L, R] if arr[i] is <= all elements between L and R. If prev_less is the previous strictly smaller index and next_less_or_equal is the next smaller-or-equal index, arr[i] contributes arr[i] * (i - prev_less) * (next_less_or_equal - i).

hints.title: Monotonic Boundary Procedure
hints.text: Use a monotonic list of indices to compute left boundaries (distance to previous strictly less element) and right boundaries (distance to next less or equal element). For each index i, multiply arr[i] by left[i] * right[i], sum over all i, and take modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def sumSubarrayMins(self, arr: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        n = len(arr)
        left = [0] * n
        right = [0] * n
        st = []
        for i in range(n):
            while st and arr[st[-1]] > arr[i]:
                st.pop()
            left[i] = i + 1 if not st else i - st[-1]
            st.append(i)
        st = []
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            while st and arr[st[-1]] >= arr[i]:
                st.pop()
            right[i] = n - i if not st else st[-1] - i
            st.append(i)
        return sum(arr[i] * left[i] * right[i] for i in range(n)) % MOD
```

variables: N: length of array arr (1 <= N <= 3 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Two monotonic passes to find left and right span boundaries.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all O(N^2) subarrays takes O(N^2) time, timing out for N = 3 * 10^4.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing boundary span arrays of size N achieves linear O(N) runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Properly handling duplicates with strict inequality on one side and non-strict inequality on the other to prevent double counting.
